name: Central Post Office
summary: The post office stands opposite the cathedral, at 2 Công trường Công xã Paris. Visit HCMC names the architects Alfred Foulhoux and Henri Auguste Vildieu and says the materials came from the Eiffel company. Vietnam Tourism says the architect is sometimes wrongly credited as Gustave Eiffel and that the design was based on his blueprints. Both sentences stay. Do not pick one.
timeNeeded: A short stop on the cathedral walk. Check on arrival.
fee: Vietnam Tourism says admission is free. Check on arrival.
getThere: With the cathedral, on the same square.
heroCaption: The post office facade and the clock, from the square

notice.title: The architect is not one name
notice.body: Visit HCMC names Foulhoux and Vildieu. Vietnam Tourism says Gustave Eiffel is sometimes given the credit in error, and that the design was based on his blueprints. Neither page is dropped.

body: Visit HCMC places the building at 2 Công trường Công xã Paris, Phường Sài Gòn, and says the interior is like the Gare d’Orsay. Visit HCMC says not to miss two painted maps at the main door, Saigon and the surroundings in 1892 and Nam Kỳ in 1936. Vietnam Tourism mentions historic maps, wooden phone booths, and a portrait of Hồ Chí Minh. Souvenir stalls line the corridors.

The address on the national account is 2 Cong xa Paris, Ben Nghe, District 1. Phường Sài Gòn and Ben Nghe both stay. Vietnam Tourism says admission is free. Check on arrival. The city itinerary pairs the stop with the morning look at the cathedral. Visit HCMC prints about 2.6 km from the Jade Emperor Pagoda.
